result.summary: The image shows a mixed-use urban intersection with a marked zebra crosswalk and sidewalks on both sides. While basic infrastructure like curb ramps and street lighting is present, the crossing lacks active traffic control or physical speed reduction measures.

hazards.name: Uncontrolled Crossing
hazards.description: The marked crosswalk lacks signals or stop signs to manage vehicle flow and prioritize pedestrians.

interventions.description: Elevate the crosswalk to the level of the sidewalk to slow traffic and increase pedestrian visibility.

result.summary: The intersection is equipped with traffic signals and marked zebra crosswalks, providing a basic level of pedestrian infrastructure. However, the lack of visible dedicated pedestrian signals and the relatively wide, open roadway design may encourage higher vehicle speeds and increase pedestrian exposure.

hazards.name: Lack of Pedestrian Signals
hazards.description: No dedicated pedestrian walk/don't-walk signals are visible, forcing pedestrians to rely on vehicular signal timing which may not be optimized for walking speeds.

hazards.name: Wide Crossing Exposure
hazards.description: The wide, undivided roadway increases the time pedestrians spend in the path of potential vehicular traffic without a refuge.
hazards.location_in_image: Foreground crosswalk across the main road

interventions.title: Pedestrian Countdown Signals
interventions.description: Install dedicated pedestrian signal heads with countdown timers to provide clear information on remaining crossing time.
